subject: Dedicated GPU queue assignments, grace periods, and committed windows (EdgeCommerce)
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@edgecommerce.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: tom.erickson@edgecommerce.com
Date: 2026-12-20T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Request: dedicated scheduling / committed windows for Q1 launch

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re moving quickly toward our Q1 launch and want to lock down committed capacity behavior for the Dedicated plan in the signed SOW. Two asks: 

1) We need a hard window (daily 06:00-22:00 PST) where our fleet receives guaranteed minimum throughput (tokens/sec) for inference to meet traffic spikes during business hours.
2) A grace-period policy that allows short bursts beyond committed baseline for 15-minute intervals without preemption during those windows.

Attached is the updated SOW and a rough CSV of our expected daily profile. Can you confirm this is feasible with Redwood Dedicated? If not, what alternatives / tapering would you propose?

Tom is on copy and will handle procurement steps — we’d like to finalize scheduling and any credits or upsell considerations this week.

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Platform Engineering
EdgeCommerce

Attachments: Edge_SOW_v3.pdf (application/pdf), requested_capacity_schedule.csv (text/csv)

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@edgecommerce.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-20T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated scheduling / committed windows for Q1 launch

Marta — thanks for the SOW and the profile. Quick read: the ask is reasonable but we need to align on two things operationally before we commit in the SOW:

- Queue assignment semantics: whether EdgeCommerce gets isolated GPU pools (full preemption protection) or a high-priority queue on shared pools. The latter is cheaper but has preemption risk during extreme contention.
- Grace period enforcement and billing: short bursts (15m) are implementable via a burst token bank tied to the committed baseline; we should decide if bursts consume committed headroom after N bursts per day.

Proposal (fast path):
1) During your requested window (06:00-22:00 PST), we attach an "elevated-priority" routing policy to your routes. That gives you queue precedence and best-effort isolation for the first X tokens/min.
2) Implement a 15-minute soft-burst bucket that allows 2 bursts/day without billing at overage rates; additional bursts will bill at overage price but will be subject to preemption only if overall system load > 95%.
3) If you require absolute non-preemptive behavior, we can move you to dedicated pool slices (cost delta in SOW).

Ben / Laura — I’m looping you in because we’ll need capacity scheduling and legal/finance sign-off on the billing rules. Marta — if you’re okay with the soft-burst model I’ll draft a short change order to the SOW (DocuSign link below).

Jasmine Liu
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.ai

Related: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/EDGE-2026-77

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai; laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: tom.erickson@edgecommerce.com; marta.ruiz@edgecommerce.com
Date: 2026-12-20T13:02:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: dedicated scheduling / committed windows for Q1 launch

Folks — forwarding the ask. Two operational constraints to flag (internal):

1) On the fleet side we’re at 86% committed utilization for the week of Jan 4 due to overlapping renewals. If we push EdgeCommerce into a non-preemptive dedicated slice we’ll need to shift other low-priority customers or activate burst capacity (expensive).
2) The new elevated-priority queue requires a small runtime change to routing config (can ship in 48 hours), but the enforcement of the 95% system-wide preemption threshold needs Product + Runtime agreement.

As a mitigation I suggest: 1) offer EdgeCommerce the soft-burst model Jasmine proposed with explicit burst caps, and 2) include a credit schedule for the first month if any preemption occurs in their peak window (credits instead of SLA exceptions). That gives them perceived guarantee without reallocating slices.

I’ll pull utilization heatmaps and a quick cost delta for the SOW change. Attaching the CSV from the customer for reference.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference

Attachments: requested_capacity_schedule.csv

From: Tom Erickson <tom.erickson@edgecommerce.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai; jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: marta.ruiz@edgecommerce.com; laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-20T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated scheduling / committed windows for Q1 launch

Thanks Ben — appreciate the quick context. From EdgeCommerce’s side:

- Soft-burst model is acceptable as long as we get a written credit policy for the first 60 days post-launch that effectively insures our peak windows. We can accept that some preemption occurs outside of the daily window.
- If there’s a clear cost delta for dedicated slices, let’s see the numbers; we may accept a higher price for absolute non-preemptive guarantees for initial 3 months.

We need the change order and an estimate by Wednesday (2026-12-23) to keep procurement moving.

Tom Erickson
VP Product, EdgeCommerce

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Tom Erickson <tom.erickson@edgecommerce.com>; marta.ruiz@edgecommerce.com
Cc: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai; ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-21T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated scheduling / committed windows for Q1 launch

Tom / Marta — agreed next steps and final decisioning path: 

1) Jasmine will prepare a one-paragraph change order for the SOW describing the soft-burst policy, burst caps (2/day at no overage), and credit terms for preemption during the first 60 days.
2) Ben will provide a cost delta for the dedicated slice vs. soft-burst, plus utilization heatmaps and the expected impact on our Jan fleet.
3) Legal/Finance will review the one-paragraph change order and the credit language; if acceptable we’ll route the DocuSign to EdgeCommerce by 2026-12-23 EOD.

We’ll treat this as an escalation because of the launch timeline; I’m marking this as high priority internally.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Operations, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
